$comment: Standing platform test checklist — area ledger. Hand-edited, append-only; validated by scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs (pnpm check:platform-checklist). Authoring rules: docs/qa/platform-checklist/README.md · execution protocol: RUNNER.md.
title: Internationalization

items.title: Notification mark-as-read is server-authoritative, the deep-link target is localized — and the title is the flow-authored literal string, because notification copy has no translation group
personas: zh-CN session user receiving an app-flow notification
en session recipient (the control that proves the title is recipient-INDEPENDENT)

requires: the showcase config declares i18n.supportedLocales ['en', 'zh-CN'] (examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts) — the zh-CN session is stock, no extra fixture
a second user to assign work to, so the assignment notification has a recipient distinct from the actor
knownGaps: the INLINE notification title this item drives is not localized, and the item pins that contract instead of assuming the retired one: `notifications` is a RETIRED top-level translation key whose own spec guidance reads "`notifications` is the retired object-first dialect — notifications have no translation group, omit them" (packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts), and the notify node renders its inline `title` slot per run from {{ }} placeholders with no locale lookup — its own config schema calls the slot "Not localizable — use template for per-locale content" (packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts). Per-recipient localized copy DOES exist on the app-flow path, through the OTHER slot: a notify node that names a `template` (with templateData) instead of an inline title is rendered per recipient at delivery, by the inbox channel and the email channel alike, in the recipient's own sys_user.locale, else the deployment default (#13881; packages/services/service-messaging/src/inbox-channel.ts). The showcase's notify_assignee authors an inline title, so its bell entry is the same literal string in every locale. sys_user.locale exists, and the avatar-menu language switcher writes it. Platform-side assignment notifications moved to app-authored flows in #3403, pinned by packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.test.ts ('does NOT emit an assignment notification when an owner field is set'). ⛔ Do not re-assert a localized-title premise for an INLINE title

the one platform notification path that IS per-recipient localized is a DIFFERENT producer, and knowing it is what stops the over-correction: plugin-audit's collab.mention writer resolves messages.mentionedYou per recipient (resolveWriteLocale(tenantId, uid) → the ADR-0053 localization context) through the long-declared `messages` translation group (packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts + src/translations/messages.ts). That is a plugin-emitted title through an existing group — not a `notifications` group, and not the app-flow path this item drives. 'Notification titles are never localized' is as wrong as 'the bell title should be localized'

steps: boot the showcase under os dev/standalone and sign in as admin

put the RECIPIENT in Chinese the way a user does: signed in as the recipient, pick 中文 in the avatar-menu language switcher, which writes the recipient's own sys_user.locale (zh-CN) and the console's UI locale together (objectui packages/app-shell/src/layout/LocaleSwitcher.tsx). The server-side equivalent is the recipient's own PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_user/RECIPIENT_ID {"locale":"zh-CN"} followed by a reload. Seeding browser storage alone is not a language switch — it leaves sys_user.locale empty (i18n.studio-follows-app-locale step 0 records the harness gap that cost a run)

read the showcase flow's notify-node config first (examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts — the record-after-update flow on `assignee != previous.assignee`, notify node `notify_assignee`, topic `task.assigned`, channel inbox) and write down cfg.title verbatim (stock: 'New task assigned: {{ record.title }}'); confirm the node authors an inline `title` and no `template`. The title expectation is that literal template with its {{ record.* }} placeholders rendered, derived from the flow, not from a locale

trigger it by changing a seeded showcase_task's assignee to the recipient. ⛔ Not `collab.assignment` — the kernel stopped emitting assignment notifications in #3403; that topic survives only in regression pins
sign in as the recipient (own browser context — never a shared tab), open the bell, and screenshot the notification entry
click through the notification's deep link and screenshot the target detail page

capture the mark-as-read request (POST /api/v1/notifications/read) and the server's unread count before and after: `unreadCount` on GET /api/v1/notifications. ⛔ Never the header badge: it counts unread notifications PLUS pending approvals (the inbox popover's approvals segment), so a pending approval holds it above zero after a clear that worked

reload the page fully and re-read the unread count from the server — and when unreadCount stays above zero, check the surviving rows' createdAt before calling it a failed clear (#7640's residual badge was NEW mail from the showcase digest flow, which fires every minute)
repeat the trigger for a recipient on an EN session and capture that bell entry as the recipient-independence control

acceptance.clause: the bell entry's title is the flow-authored literal string with its {{ record.* }} placeholders rendered — an INLINE notification title is NOT localized, and this clause pins the shipped contract rather than the retired one
acceptance.verify: the bell entry renders exactly cfg.title from the showcase flow's notify node with its {{ record.title }} placeholder rendered (stock showcase: 'New task assigned: ' followed by the task's title), character for character, on a zh-CN session. The node renders an inline title with no locale lookup, so an English title on a Chinese session is the PASS here. A raw, unrendered '{{ record.title }}' token IS a FAIL — rendering, not translation, is what this clause tests
acceptance.evidence: bell screenshot next to the flow's notify-node config

acceptance.clause: the deep-link target renders in zh-CN — the click-through lands on a localized page, not a mixed-language one
acceptance.verify: detail-page screenshot in zh-CN (translated object label, field labels, section labels)

acceptance.clause: mark-as-read actually clears the unread state — the notifications REST routes must be mounted on the server actually serving os dev (the #3362 dispatcher-only registration made the console 404 here while unit tests stayed green)
acceptance.verify: POST /api/v1/notifications/read returns 2xx on the running server and a fresh unreadCount read (GET /api/v1/notifications) drops. Read the server's unreadCount, never the header badge, which adds pending approvals
acceptance.evidence: the network trace + before/after unread count

acceptance.clause: the cleared state is authoritative — it survives a full reload, proving the server persisted it rather than the client repainting
acceptance.verify: after a hard reload, the server's unread count still reflects the read (no resurrection of the cleared item)

acceptance.clause: the title is recipient-INDEPENDENT: the same event notifies an EN-session and a zh-CN-session recipient with the identical title string — the showcase flow authors an INLINE title, which the notify node renders with no locale lookup. Per-recipient copy exists only through a notify `template` reference (rendered in each recipient's sys_user.locale at delivery), which this flow does not use
acceptance.verify: the control recipient's bell entry carries the same title string as the zh-CN recipient's, modulo the rendered record values. A DIFFERENCE is the finding in this clause — it would mean the inline title slot was localized per recipient, which its contract says it never is: confirm which producer emitted the row (the showcase flow's notify node, or a plugin writer resolving an existing group such as messages.mentionedYou) and file rather than tick. If the flow now names a `template` instead of an inline title, its per-recipient members are DECLARED and this item's premise has moved — revise the item, do not tick
acceptance.evidence: the two bell screenshots side by side

negative: a mark-as-read that returns 404/405 (routes mounted only on the dispatcher, not the live Hono server) is the #3362 regression — FAIL, and unit-test greenness is not a defense

filing a bug because the bell title renders English on a Chinese session is the misread this item now forecloses (#7684): the title is app-authored literal copy and the platform declares no translation group for it. The finding in that direction is a per-recipient DIFFERENCE, not an English title

authoring a `notifications` key to 'fix' the title is a FAIL of the fix, not of the platform — the key is retired at both translation doors and i18n.strict-translation-key-rejection is the item that proves the rejection
source: examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts#supportedLocales (supportedLocales)
packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts#TRANSLATION_KEY_GUIDANCE (TRANSLATION_KEY_GUIDANCE — `notifications` is the retired object-first dialect; notifications have no translation group)
#3403 (platform-side assignment notifications moved to app-authored flows; pinned by packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.test.ts)
examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts#notify_assignee (the notify_assignee node whose literal cfg.title this item now asserts)

packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts#title (the inline title is rendered per run from {{ }} placeholders with no locale lookup — the node schema calls it 'Not localizable'; the localizable path is the `template` slot)

packages/services/service-messaging/src/inbox-channel.ts (a notify `template` reference is rendered per recipient at delivery, in the recipient's sys_user.locale else the deployment default, #13881 — the per-recipient path this item's inline-title flow does not take)
#7684 (the decision this revision implements), #7640 (the run that surfaced it)

history.change: initial import from #3358; the #3362 route-seam regression is the reason the oracle is a live-server network trace, never a unit test
expanded to deep-test contract: concrete steps, multi-clause acceptance, negatives, variants

c0/c4 REWRITTEN against the shipped contract (#7684). Both clauses assumed a per-recipient localized notification title — a capability the spec retired — so on a stock app they were unprovable and landed blocked(fixture) rather than testing anything. c0 now asserts the flow-authored literal title with its placeholders interpolated; c4 now asserts the title is recipient-INDEPENDENT, with a per-recipient difference as the finding. The mechanical read/clear clauses (live-server POST /notifications/read + the survives-reload re-read) are untouched and remain the item's substance. The retirement is cited on the item (translation.zod.ts, #3403, notify-node.ts) so the next author cannot re-assert the retired premise; the steps drop the unperformable 'set the recipient user's locale' (sys_user has no locale field) and the stale collab.assignment trigger. Verified before editing: the retirement guidance is still on origin/main and no notification-copy translation group has appeared — plugin-audit's per-recipient collab.mention title resolves the pre-existing `messages` group, a different producer, and is recorded in knownGaps so the correction does not overshoot

knownGaps[0], steps[1] and [2], acceptance[0] (clause, verify) and acceptance[4] (clause, verify) and source[7] re-pointed (checklist-accuracy note 1 of QA run #23951, wave #23878). Three premises had moved: sys_user.locale exists and the avatar-menu switcher writes it (zh-CN accepted), so steps[1]'s storage-only, language-code-only recipe is replaced by the switcher (or the recipient's own PATCH of sys_user.locale); the notify node gained a per-recipient `template` path (#13881), so 'per-recipient localization is spec-RETIRED' is wrong — only the INLINE title is unlocalized, which is what the showcase flow uses; and placeholders are {{ record.title }}, so the FAIL shape is an unrendered double-brace token. The clauses are not loosened: clause 0 still demands the literal rendered title, and clause 4 still files any per-recipient difference on an inline title; a flow that moved to a `template` is a premise change that revises the item, never a tick

steps[6], steps[7] and acceptance[2].verify read the server's unreadCount (GET /api/v1/notifications), never the header badge (checklist-accuracy finding of QA run #25817, release-18.2.0-manual-set at 6679644a; wave anchor #25807): the badge counts notifications plus pending approvals, so a pending approval reads as a failed clear. The clauses are unchanged

items.title: Studio follows the in-app locale switch — no mixed-language session

requires: the console's own zh catalogue for the Studio designers: the object editor's section and field labels are objectui's metadata-admin `designer.object.*` strings (objectui packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts, read by inspectors/ObjectDefaultInspector.tsx), NOT the served metadataForms translation group — QA run #23951 read 标识、显示名与分类 / 显示名 where the served group carries …分类标签 / 显示名称. The metadataForms group stays platform-owned (platform-objects translates it, and scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs folds that baseline away)
knownGaps: the showcase's declared surface carries FROZEN untranslated debt, ratcheted by scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs + scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json (examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts: 414 untranslated declared labels in scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json, held flat — growth fails the gate, and the count only shrinks). Residual English strings on an otherwise-Chinese Studio surface (#7640 recorded `Announcement`, `Business Unit`, `Owning Business Unit`, `Sales Region`) render their EN SOURCE label, never a raw key, and are legitimate — exactly as i18n.surface-matrix's knownGaps already declares for the same fixture. This item asserts consistency WITH the bundle, not 100% coverage

steps: sign in as admin on the showcase, switch the in-app locale to zh-CN, and confirm the app shell followed (nav in zh-CN). To switch, use the avatar-menu language switcher (it writes the user's locale); seeding browser storage alone is not a language switch — a run that only seeds the UI language in browser storage leaves the user's stored locale empty, so dates follow the browser and a FAIL read off it is the harness's, not the product's
navigate into Studio / metadata-admin: open the object editor for showcase_project and the dashboard designer for showcase_chart_gallery

screenshot the object editor's form — its section and field labels come from objectui's metadata-admin catalogue (`designer.object.*` in ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts, in this checkout), not from the served metadataForms translation group (packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts): judge them against that catalogue (e.g. section 基础信息 with hint 标识、显示名与分类)

screenshot a surface showing RELATIVE dates in the switched locale: the Studio Data pillar's records grid (/_console/studio/<package>/data, an object's records), whose timestamps render as '6天前'-style relative forms. The metadata list and history surfaces show none — history renders absolute timestamps — so they cannot score this step
reload the browser fully and re-screenshot one Studio surface — the locale choice must survive the reload
switch back to en through the same avatar-menu language switcher and re-screenshot the same two Studio surfaces

acceptance.clause: Studio's metadata-editor forms render in the switched locale — for the object editor through objectui's own metadata-admin catalogue (`designer.object.*`), which is where its strings come from; the served metadataForms group is not what this editor renders
acceptance.verify: object-editor screenshot shows zh-CN section and field labels that match objectui's metadata-admin catalogue at the pin (e.g. section 基础信息, hint 标识、显示名与分类), not English

acceptance.clause: no mixed-language session in the sense the coverage ratchet defines: every string the bundle DOES translate renders translated, and any string it does not renders its EN SOURCE label — never a raw dotted key. The showcase's frozen untranslated debt is legitimate here, not a FAIL
acceptance.verify: review each captured Studio screenshot in two passes: (a) no dotted key path anywhere — that is an unconditional FAIL; (b) every residual English string sitting next to Chinese ones is checked against the frozen debt ratcheted by scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs + scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json — a string inside that debt is expected and ticks, a string the bundle DOES translate rendering English is the FAIL. User data (record values) is exempt
acceptance.evidence: the annotated screenshots + the coverage-baseline reading each residual English string was judged against

acceptance.clause: relative dates follow the locale
acceptance.verify: the Studio Data pillar's records-grid timestamps render zh-CN relative forms (e.g. 6天前) after the switch, and English relative forms after the switch back; the metadata list / history surfaces carry absolute timestamps and are not this clause's subject

acceptance.clause: the locale choice persists across a full reload — it is stored, not a transient client state
acceptance.verify: post-reload Studio screenshot is still zh-CN without re-selecting

acceptance.clause: switching back to en restores English on the same surfaces — the switch is symmetric, not a one-way ratchet
acceptance.verify: the return-to-en screenshots show the same surfaces fully in English

negative: a Studio surface staying English after the app switched (mixed session) is the FAIL this item exists for — judged against the bundle, not by counting English words: a string the bundle feeding that surface translates (the console's metadata-admin catalogue for the Studio designers, the app's bundle for app labels such as navigation) rendering English is the FAIL; a string inside the frozen coverage debt rendering its EN source label is not. Check against a fresh objectui build before filing either way (the vendored /_console bundle may be stale)
source: packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts#metadataForms (metadataForms group + resolveMetadataFormLabels convention — the served group, which the Studio object editor does not render)

objectui packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts (the `designer.object.*` zh strings) + inspectors/ObjectDefaultInspector.tsx (the object editor that reads them) — where the object editor's labels come from (QA run #23951, checklist-accuracy note 3)
scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs#baseline (platform metadata-form baseline is platform-objects-owned)
scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json (the frozen per-config untranslated counts this item's mixed-language clause is judged against)
#7640 (i18n area run — the residual EN strings that exposed the clause/ratchet collision), #7686
#21782 (re-run comment: the held relative-date FAIL was a harness gap — browser storage seeded, switcher never used; PASS through the avatar-menu switcher)

history.change: initial import from #3358
expanded to deep-test contract: concrete steps, multi-clause acceptance, negatives, variants

the mixed-language clause is reconciled with the coverage ratchet (#7640): as written it read 'no untranslated declared string next to translated ones', which the showcase's FROZEN untranslated debt violates by design — the sibling item i18n.surface-matrix already declares that debt legitimate, so this item contradicted it and cost a clean PASS. The clause now judges against the bundle (translated key renders translated; untranslated key renders its EN SOURCE label; a raw dotted key is the unconditional FAIL), the same knownGap is declared on this item's fixtures, and the negative carries the matching qualifier

the switch steps now name HOW to switch: through the avatar-menu language switcher, which writes the user's locale. Seeding browser storage alone is not a language switch. The 17.7 console run held a relative-date FAIL on this item, and its re-run on #21782 settled it as a harness gap: the first lane had set the UI language only in browser storage, so the user's stored locale stayed empty and dates followed the browser. Through the switcher the clause passed, so the clauses themselves are unchanged (card #21851 entry 11, filed with the follow-up run #21845)

steps[3] and acceptance[2].verify re-pointed to the surface that renders relative dates (stale step, #23163 A2; parked on #23121, carried by #23169). The metadata list and history surfaces carry no relative dates — history is absolute — so the step pointed at nothing scorable. QA run #23163 read relative dates (6天前) on the Studio Data pillar's records grid under zh-CN, through the avatar-menu switcher, and passed

knownGaps[0], fixtures.requires[0], steps[2], acceptance[0] (clause, verify), negative[0] and source re-pointed (checklist-accuracy notes 2 and 3 of QA run #23951, wave #23878). The clause-0 premise was wrong: the Studio object editor's strings come from objectui's metadata-admin catalogue (designer.object.* in packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts, ObjectDefaultInspector.tsx), not the served metadataForms group — #23951 read 标识、显示名与分类 / 显示名 where the group carries …分类标签 / 显示名称 — so the clause passed on its verify text while naming the wrong source, and negative[0] judged residual English against the wrong bundle. Both now name the catalogue that feeds the surface. The frozen debt count is 414, not 451 (scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json). Not loosened: a zh session still FAILS on any English string the feeding bundle translates, and on any raw dotted key

items.title: Every translatable surface localizes on a zh-CN session — one pass over the full translation-group vocabulary, plus the runtime i18n routes it resolves through

requires: the showcase translation bundle (examples/app-showcase/src/system/translations/index.ts) — it deliberately covers EVERY field surfaced as a list column so a zh-CN list never mixes locales
platform-objects' own bundles for sys_ object labels and Studio metadataForms (platform-owned per scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs)
knownGaps: the showcase's declared surface carries FROZEN untranslated debt, ratcheted by scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs + i18n-coverage-baseline.json — expect some declared strings to legitimately fall back to en; the per-surface check is 'translated keys render translated, untranslated keys render the SOURCE label (never a raw dotted key)', not 100% coverage

objects._views.<view>.emptyState WAS unafforded and no longer is: the #7714 specimen has landed. examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/task.view.ts authors an emptyState on the `urgent` view (its comment block cites #7714) and src/system/translations/index.ts carries the zh-CN half under objects.showcase_task._views.urgent.emptyState.{title,message}. The variant is runnable; the only setup it needs is an empty `urgent` view (demote the two urgent seed rows)

objects._sections is addressable ONLY on sections that declare a `name` (packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts: a nameless section renders its authored label in every locale; packages/lint's translation-section-name-missing rule nudges authors toward the name). On the stock showcase every surface this item reads declares one: showcase_task's DEFAULT form (the New/Edit form, section `task`), the task record page — examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/task-detail.page.ts's record:details block names its sections overview / schedule / details since #22036, reusing objects.showcase_task._sections — and showcase_contact's default form. QA run #23163 read all three in zh under zh-CN, so the old reading (the record page renders EN in every locale) is stale. ⚠ The named formViews tabbed / wizard / split are reachable from NO console door: `…/showcase_task/view/tabbed` is a LIST-view route and renders the grid (records-forms.form-view-gallery says why), so do not read _sections there

acceptance[5]'s CONFIRM half has no stock specimen at all, so on stock it is PIN-ONLY (QA run #21782 recorded it blocked(fixture) as 'no zh confirmText'; parked on #22017 row 8). No showcase action declares a `confirmText` (src/ui/actions, src/data/objects; only a view's bulkActionDefs carry one, and those are not `_actions` entries), so a zh-CN bundle entry has nothing to translate. Score it from the objectui pins in `automated`. The toast half stays live (e.g. showcase_recalc_estimate's zh successMessage). A live confirm specimen would need a scratch-package action declaring confirmText plus a translation overlay (translation is runtime-writable); that is not run-proven

steps: before the browser: read the served translation metadata (GET /api/v1/meta/translation, or the bundle source) and note, per variant surface, at least one key that IS translated to zh-CN — expectations derive from data, not vibes

sign in as admin, switch to zh-CN, and walk one surface per variant, screenshotting each. To switch, use the avatar-menu language switcher (it writes the user's locale); seeding browser storage alone is not a language switch — a run that only seeds the UI language in browser storage leaves the user's stored locale empty, so dates follow the browser and a relative-dates FAIL read off it is the harness's, not the product's:
nav labels — the Showcase app sidebar groups/nodes (apps.<app>.navigation.<node_id>.label group)
list headers — the showcase_task list columns (objects.<object>.fields.<field>.label; the bundle translates every surfaced column incl. status/priority OPTION labels)
form labels + placeholders on a task edit form (fields group), and select options in the form and list filters (fields.<field>.options)
an action dialog — trigger an object action with confirmText/successMessage and capture the confirm prompt and the success toast (_actions group: label/confirmText/successMessage)

a view empty state (_views.<view>.emptyState) — RUNNABLE on the stock fixture since the #7714 specimen landed: examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/task.view.ts authors an emptyState on the filtered `urgent` view, and the zh-CN bundle carries objects.showcase_task._views.urgent.emptyState.{title,message}. Demote the two urgent seed rows (or filter them away) so the view renders empty, then read the copy — it resolves to 暂无紧急任务 / 当前没有需要立即处理的事项。任务优先级调整为「紧急」后会出现在这里。 ⛔ Still do not manufacture coverage from the console's built-in zero-row placeholder, which is console chrome and not an objects._views.<view>.emptyState resolution

section labels (_sections group) — read them off a NAMED-section surface the console actually renders: showcase_task's New form (its default form's `task` section), a task record page (task-detail.page.ts names overview / schedule / details since #22036) and showcase_contact's default edit form (ui/views/contact.view.ts). Each declares a stable `name` per section, which is the only thing that makes objects.<object>._sections.<name>.label resolvable — the showcase bundle carries 概览/排期/详细信息 and 联系方式/工作信息/状态/备注 for exactly those names. ⛔ Not `…/view/tabbed`: the named formViews are reachable from no console door, and that URL renders the grid (see the knownGap below)

a dashboard — Chart Gallery's title and widget titles (dashboards.<name>.label / widgets.<id>.title). The showcase bundle translates one widget title: dashboards.showcase_chart_gallery.widgets.combo_count_vs_progress.title → 任务数与平均进度 on the runtime dashboard; read that widget

a page — a page header's title/subtitle (pages.<name> group). No showcase page carries a translated title or subtitle (QA run #23951 fixture gap), so read a PLATFORM page: pages.connect_agent (label 连接智能体 and its zh subtitle, platform-objects' bundle), and the showcase_command_center page's translated component titles (pages.showcase_command_center.components.*)
a Settings namespace — title, group titles, key labels, and the source badges (settings.<namespace> + settingsCommon.sourceLabels)
Studio metadata forms (metadataForms group — overlaps i18n.studio-follows-app-locale; a pinned pass there may be cited)
a sys_ object surface — e.g. the All Users list showing sys_user's translated label (platform-objects-owned bundle)
runtime i18n routes (server truth, consulted independently of the browser — these are what the client resolves labels through): GET /api/v1/i18n/locales and record data.locales
GET /api/v1/i18n/translations/zh-CN — record whether it is non-empty and whether every key path sits under a declared translation group
GET /api/v1/i18n/labels/showcase_task/zh-CN — record its { object, locale, labels } and hold it next to the zh-CN list-header the browser rendered for showcase_task

unknown-locale probe: GET /api/v1/i18n/translations/zz-ZZ and GET /api/v1/i18n/labels/showcase_task/zz-ZZ — capture WHICH degradation the running server does (the FileI18nAdapter returns an empty {} map for an unloaded locale; getTranslations does NOT synthesize the default bundle — record the observed shape, do not assume a fallback)

feed/audit verb variant (E11): set the TENANT locale to zh-CN first (PUT /api/settings/localization {values:{locale:'zh-CN'}}), THEN trigger an activity-feed / audit entry (an assignment or a record edit) and screenshot its rendered verb/template — the verb is localized and frozen at write time, so an entry created before the flip stays in its original locale no matter which session reads it
record a per-variant verdict table with the screenshot evidence

acceptance.clause: every variant surface renders its known-translated key in zh-CN — verified per-variant, no surface inferred from a sibling
acceptance.verify: one screenshot per variant showing the pre-identified translated key rendered in zh-CN

acceptance.clause: expectations are grounded in server truth first: the translation metadata read names which keys are translated, and the screenshots are judged against THAT list
acceptance.verify: the translation read (or bundle source) is captured and each per-variant expectation cites its key

acceptance.clause: fallback is honest: an untranslated declared string renders its SOURCE-language label — never a raw dotted key path, never an empty cell
acceptance.verify: spot-check at least two known-untranslated keys — derive them as keys the showcase declares but the served zh tree lacks: scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json records only a COUNT per config (414 for examples/app-showcase at base 9a7838edf5), never a key list; each shows the en label, no 'objects.x.fields.y.label' literals anywhere in the session

acceptance.clause: select OPTION labels localize everywhere they appear: list cells, form selects, and list filters all show the translated option label for the same stored value
acceptance.verify: the showcase_task status/priority options (translated in the bundle) render zh-CN in all three places

acceptance.clause: a list of a fully-covered object never mixes locales — the bundle's own contract (it translates every surfaced column precisely to prevent 状态 next to 'Assignee')

items.title: Unknown, legacy-dialect, and retired translation keys are rejected loudly at BOTH authoring doors — never silently stripped

requires: runtime metadata authoring enabled (the `translation` item door: the Studio translation editor or the metadata API against /api/v1/meta/translation)

steps: item door — via the metadata API, attempt to save a zh-CN `translation` item carrying each variant in turn (one save per variant), always alongside one VALID key (e.g. objects.showcase_task.label) so the rejection provably targets the bad key, not the document. Name the item in snake_case (e.g. qa_strict_zh_cn) and set `locale: zh-CN`: the conventional name `zh-CN` is refused first by the item-name rule (400 INVALID_REQUEST, 'is not a legal metadata item name'), before any key is judged, so a run that keeps it never reaches the gate this item tests. The `name` describe in translation.zod.ts still calls the locale code the convention; do not follow it at this door
capture the exact error text for each attempted save
after each rejection, read the item back and record that nothing (including the valid key) was persisted by the failed save

bundle door — in a scratch script inside the worktree, call defineTranslation and defineTranslationBundle with the same variants and capture each parse error (this is the door #3778's item-only guard missed; #4001's strict shapes must cover both). ⚠️ They are NOT on the same entry point: defineTranslationBundle is re-exported from the package ROOT (@objectstack/spec), while defineTranslation resolves only through the @objectstack/spec/system subpath. Importing both from the root yields 'defineTranslation is not a function', which reads exactly like a missing guard

verify the alias suggestion channel: a near-miss key (helpText on a FIELD translation, label on a WIDGET translation) must be rejected WITH the did-you-mean pointing at the declared spelling (help; title)

verify the guidance channel: legacy object-first keys (o, app, nav, dashboard, errors, _meta) and retired validationMessages must carry their prescription (where the content belongs now, or that it has no home), not just 'unrecognized key'
save a correct version of the same content and confirm it persists and resolves (the gate rejects keys, not translations)

acceptance.clause: every variant is REJECTED at the item door with an error naming the surface and echoing the offending key
acceptance.verify: each save returns 422 INVALID_METADATA whose text contains the offending key and the surface name ('this translation', 'this field translation', …)

acceptance.clause: the same variants are rejected at the bundle door — the two doors cannot diverge (the #3778/#4522 asymmetry: covered at one door, open at the other)
acceptance.verify: defineTranslation/defineTranslationBundle throw for every variant with equivalent error content

acceptance.verify: helpText→help (field), label→title (dashboard widget) suggestions appear in the respective errors

acceptance.verify: the o/app/nav/dashboard errors point at objects./apps./navigation/dashboards (plural); validationMessages cites ADR-0049 and spec 17.0.0 (the live text reads 'removed in @objectstack/spec 17.0.0 (ADR-0049)') and names the rule-message home, object.validations[].message, translated under objects.OBJECT._validations.RULE.message

items.title: The i18n build gates hold and can go red: bundle drift, undeclared extract keys, and the coverage ratchet

requires: a BUILT workspace — both gates run the built CLI and now hard-fail with a named prerequisite verdict when it is missing (#5217/#5862) instead of blaming an innocent config

steps: build the workspace, then run node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs and capture the output (two distinct verdicts: bundle drift; undeclared extract key)

run node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --self-test and node scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs --self-test — the classifiers must be provably able to go red (#4690: a gate observed only green is indistinguishable from a gate matching nothing)
run node scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs against the baseline

prove the drift gate bites — the perturbation must be STRUCTURAL: remove or rename a KEY in one committed bundle, re-run check-i18n-bundles.mjs, capture the red verdict, then revert. Prefer perturbing OUTSIDE the repo: #7640 drove this red-then-green from a /tmp symlink farm (every workspace entry symlinked, one real copy of the package under test), so no repo file was ever touched

⛔ do NOT perturb a translation VALUE — the extract runs in merge mode, so a committed bundle is its own baseline for values and an edited string stays green BY DESIGN (check-i18n-bundles.mjs's own regenerate hint: 'Merge mode is on, so no existing translation is overwritten'; AGENTS.md §Documentation Guardrails: 'editing a string is fine, while adding or dropping keys is drift'). #7640 ran the literal value perturbation this step used to prescribe, watched the gate stay green, and only then found the structural perturbation that bites — the step is worded structurally now so the next runner does not repeat that lap or misread the green as a gate defect

prove the ratchet bites: the baseline check must fail on an INCREASED untranslated count — verify by inspecting that the current counts equal the baseline (growth would fail), and capture the baseline comparison output
in an UNBUILT state (or by consulting the gates' own prerequisite check), confirm the failure mode is the named build-prerequisite verdict, not nine phantom bundle problems

acceptance.clause: check-i18n-bundles passes on a clean tree, reporting its two verdict classes separately
acceptance.verify: exit 0 with the drift and undeclared-key sections both clean

acceptance.clause: both gates' --self-test proves the red path exists
acceptance.verify: each --self-test run exercises its classifiers against fixed samples and passes

acceptance.clause: the drift gate actually bites on STRUCTURAL drift: a bundle with a removed or renamed KEY turns the gate red naming the drifted package
acceptance.verify: the structural perturbation run exits non-zero citing the perturbed bundle; the revert run is green again. A VALUE edit is NOT a valid probe of this clause — merge mode keeps it green by design, so a green value-edit run proves nothing about the gate in either direction
acceptance.evidence: the red output + the post-revert green output

acceptance.clause: the coverage ratchet holds the frozen debt: counts match the committed baseline, and the gate's contract fails growth
acceptance.verify: check-i18n-coverage exits 0 with counts equal to scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json

acceptance.clause: an unbuilt workspace produces the HARD named prerequisite failure ('measured nothing'), never a skip and never phantom per-config errors
acceptance.verify: the prerequisite verdict names the missing build, not an i18n config

negative: a green run after the deliberate STRUCTURAL perturbation (removed/renamed key) is a FAIL of the gate itself — file against the gate, and do not trust any of its other verdicts that sweep

a green run after a VALUE edit is NOT a finding and must never be filed as one — merge mode makes the committed bundle its own baseline for values, so that green is the designed behaviour (#7640 nearly filed it)
--write printing 'regenerated' while writing nothing (the historical unbuilt-CLI shape) is a FAIL

scripts/check-i18n-coverage.mjs (#3370 declared-surface ratchet, #5862 prerequisite check)
scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json
AGENTS.md §Documentation Guardrails, the translations/*.generated.ts row (merge-mode extract ⇒ values are hand-written and expected to differ; adding or dropping keys is the drift)
#7640 (i18n area run — the value perturbation stayed green; the structural one went red-then-green)

history.change: new item: the i18n build lane — drift gate, undeclared-key gate, ratchet, and their provable red paths

step 4 was a no-op as written: 'perturb one committed bundle VALUE' is green by design under merge mode, where the committed file is its own baseline. Reworded to the STRUCTURAL perturbation (remove/rename a KEY) that actually bites, split into a do/don't pair, with the #7640 symlink-farm technique that drives it without touching a repo file; the drift-bites clause and both negatives are reconciled so a green value edit can no longer be read (or filed) as a gate defect
